ranking_note: Authored from the before descriptions at commit b4214d6c7ea542bbcc1402639343e967ac6a0abf, frozen before any rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. Competitors are github:advise (forward-looking design and setup of a settings area, where audit reviews the current state and drift) and github:setup (user-invoked only: checks gh install and auth and writes the plugin's consumer config). audit owns the read-only, current-state review of the GitHub settings and admin plane: drift from declared conventions, standards conformance and cost signals.

Review our org's billing settings: spending limits, paid seats, Actions minutes. Is anything costing more than it should?
List every webhook and installed GitHub App across the org and tell me which ones look stale or over-permissioned.
Check the fine-grained tokens and deploy keys our org has granted and tell me what's risky right now.
Is secret scanning and Dependabot actually turned on everywhere in the org, or are some repos missing it?
Which third-party actions are workflows in our org permitted to run at the moment? Anything there that shouldn't be?
Compare the default-branch protection on our five service repos and tell me where they differ.
Give me a findings report on our GitHub organization's admin settings against GitHub's current recommendations.

Go through all my open pull requests and push each one forward.
